newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SPP gas signs DM 270 mln, 5-yr synd loan. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Slovak SPP gas signs DM 270 mln, 5-yr synd loan. [CORRECTED 13:40 GMT]

text.p: Slovak state-run gas distributor SPP s.p. said on Friday it had signed a DM 270 million, five-year syndicated loan with lead arrangers Citibank London and ING Barings London.
(Corrects to add ING Barings as a lead arranger)
The credit facility, with ING Barings London co-lead arranger, was priced at 35 basis points over LIBOR and does not require any third-party guarantee, an SPP statement said.

"Funds from the credit will be used for financing SPP's main investment activities, including completion of the fifth line of gas pipeline transporting Russian gas to western Europe," SPP spokesman Lubomir Rabay told Reuters during the signing ceremony in Bratislava.
The syndication includes 17 banks from nine countries. Neither SPP officials, nor Citibank representatives would disclose names of participating banks.
"The originally proposed sum for the loan was 200 million marks, but due to heavy interest among banks in the syndication, the final amount was increased to 270 million," Rabay said.

SPP is one of the most profitable Slovak companies, with a 1996 net profit of 8.862 billion crowns on revenues totalling around 48 billion crowns. The company recorded a net profit of 6.467 billion crowns in 1995.
Most of its revenues come from transit fees on Russian gas to western Europe, which last year totalled around 80 billion cubic metres.

The pipeline, which began operation in April 1971, serves 10 major consumers in central and western Europe. Russia pays for the transfer by supplying about four billion cubic metres of gas to Slovak consumers, which covers about two-thirds of domestic annual consumption.

The fifth line of the gas pipeline, currently under cosntruction, is planned to increase the Slovakia's annual gas transport capacity to around 90 billion cubic metres when it becomes fully operational in the year 2000.
